Diane Ortiz, a teller at the Lakeside Credit Union branch on Fifth Street, has been charged with embezzling more than $40,000 from customer accounts over an eight-month period, prosecutors announced Wednesday. According to the criminal complaint, Ortiz altered internal transfer records to route small amounts from dormant accounts into a personal account she controlled.

The scheme was uncovered during a routine quarterly audit, which flagged a pattern of transfers inconsistent with normal account activity. Branch manager Louis Ferreira placed Ortiz on unpaid leave immediately after the discrepancies were confirmed and notified both law enforcement and the credit union's regional compliance office.

As part of the review, auditors interviewed several other employees who had worked the same shifts as Ortiz, including fellow teller Kevin Park, who was on duty at the adjacent window during the period in question. Park was not accused of any wrongdoing; auditors said he was interviewed as a standard part of confirming that till counts and transaction logs from his own window matched normal patterns, which they did. Park told auditors he had not noticed anything unusual about Ortiz's till during the period covered by the investigation.

Ortiz is scheduled to be arraigned next month. The credit union said it has since implemented additional transfer-verification steps to prevent similar activity in the future.

Diane Ortiz, the former Lakeside Credit Union teller who pleaded guilty to embezzling more than $40,000 from customer accounts, was sentenced Tuesday to three years of probation and ordered to pay full restitution. The judge cited Ortiz's lack of prior record and her cooperation with investigators in imposing a sentence below the standard guideline range.

During the sentencing hearing, prosecutors summarized testimony gathered during the investigation, including brief statements from coworkers about standard till-reconciliation procedures at the branch. Kevin Park, another teller who worked alongside Ortiz, had provided a short written statement earlier in the case describing how till counts were normally logged at the end of each shift; he was not called to testify in person and was not named as a witness to any of the specific transfers at issue.

Credit union regional director Priya Nair said the institution was satisfied with the outcome and reiterated that no other employee had been found to have any involvement in the scheme. Ortiz declined to comment as she left the courthouse.

Lakeside Credit Union hosted a free financial literacy class for local families at its Fifth Street branch on Saturday, covering topics such as budgeting, building credit, and avoiding common banking fees. The class was led by branch staff, including teller Kevin Park, who walked attendees through a sample monthly budget worksheet.

About twenty residents attended the session, which the credit union said it plans to offer quarterly going forward. Park fielded questions from attendees about how to read a monthly account statement and answered a handful of questions about setting up automatic savings transfers.

Branch manager Louis Ferreira said the credit union sees the classes as part of its community outreach efforts and hopes to expand the program to include a session focused on first-time homebuyers later in the year.
